CRI / FENTANYL

Fentanyl CRI

Uses the shared species and weight above. Workbook profiles & clinical references.

Best use: Short-acting opioid infusion for titratable analgesia; reassess pain, sedation, breathing and heart rate. Practice reference.

Prepare a syringe

Linked preparation: dose × weight ÷ concentration = pump rate; final volume ÷ pump rate = hours. Use the optional shortcut or customize the fields below.

The shortcut sets pump rate equal to the selected dose (for example, 3 mcg/kg/hr → 3 mL/hr). All preparation fields remain editable.

Perianaesthetic reference: dogs 3–6; cats 2–5 mcg/kg/hr. The existing workbook prefill of 1 is retained for review; select the prescribed dose. No loading dose included.

Changing pump rate keeps dose and final volume fixed, and recalculates concentration and hours. Changing dose or concentration recalculates pump rate and hours. Changing hours adjusts final volume at the current rate. These inputs plan a NEW preparation; keep an existing syringe’s concentration fixed when titrating. Defaults: 12 mL final at 1 mL/hr before priming/discard.

Worked math

More info · concentration options

Workbook comparison concentrations are 12.5, 25 and 50 mcg/mL. The optional shortcut produces a prepared concentration numerically equal to weight in kg (mcg/mL), so 1 mL/hr delivers 1 mcg/kg/hr. Custom pump rates produce other concentrations. Changing inputs calculates a new preparation; titrate an existing syringe by keeping its concentration fixed. Review compatibility, stability, pump accuracy, measurable stock volume and line priming under your hospital protocol. Preparation volume is the measured final volume, before priming/discard.

Practice source

Perianaesthetic Analgesic Guidelines, fentanyl, page 22: short duration supports infusion use; dog/cat dose references and adverse-effect precautions. This perianaesthetic reference is not a universal ER dose protocol. Best-use wording is a clinical summary.
